offence_severity: Death (Section 302) - Minimum 10 years, Maximum Life Imprisonment; Robbery (Section 392) - Minimum 3 years, Maximum 7 years
physical_harm: Death of the deceased caused by the appellant
financial_property_loss: Rs. 100/150, Rs. 15000/-, Rs. 2,50,000/-, mobile phone, jewels, ornaments, ear rings, necklace
key_evidence_accepted: The conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant does not call for interference. The sequence of events, as per the prosecution, was consistently maintained by complainant - PW.17 before the Court which was fully supported by the other eye-witnesses, namely, PWs.19, 20, 23 and 25. PW 20 was not treated as a hostile witness in spite of diametrically opposite version stated by him as regards the identity of the appellant. Nevertheless, both the Courts below proceeded to hold that the identity made by PW.20 could not be ignored. The trial court adjourned the case for cross-examination of PW.20 by two months on the request on behalf of the appellant and according to the High Court such a long adjournment provided scope for maneuvering.
witness_credibility: PW 20 was not treated as a hostile witness in spite of diametrically opposite version stated by him as regards the identity of the appellant. Nevertheless, both the Courts below proceeded to hold that the identity made by PW.20 could not be ignored.
trial_duration: The trial court convicted the appellant and co-accused for offences under Sections 302/34 and 392/34 IPC. The High Court confirmed the conviction of the appellant. The conviction of the co-accused under Section 392/34 IPC was confirmed while he was acquitted under Section 302/34 IPC. The appeal was dismissed by the Supreme Court.
legal_representation: Subramonium Prasad, Rajat Khattry and Varun Tandon for the Appellant. B. Chahar, P.K. Dey, Sadhana Sandhu, B.V. Balramdas and Anil Katiyar for the Respondent.
investigation_status: The appellant and co-accused were arrested under the Arms Act. A search was conducted, and a loaded pistol and live cartridges were recovered from them. Further recoveries were made from the appellant, namely, a gold chain and a 'Rado' wrist watch. The investigation revealed that they were involved in the incident on 27.10.1998 at the residence of Shama Parveen.
procedural_irregularity: The trial court adjourned the case for two months for cross-examination of PW.20, which was considered a violation of the provisions under Sections 231 and 309 Cr.P.C. The High Court noted that such a long adjournment provided scope for maneuvering.
appeal_history: The trial court convicted the appellant and co-accused. The High Court confirmed the conviction of the appellant and acquitted the co-accused under Section 302/34 IPC. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant and co-accused entered the house of the complainant armed with revolvers and a knife, snatched valuables, and that the appellant shot the deceased after attempting to molest the complainant. The prosecution relied on eye-witness accounts, recovery of stolen items, and identification of the accused.
defence_argument: The appellant contended that the reliance on PW 20's identification was not correct as he turned hostile during cross-examination, and that the recovery of articles from the accused was not justified.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that courts dealing with serious offences must proceed with trials on a day-to-day basis to ensure speedy justice and prevent undue adjournments.
precedent_relied_upon: Rajdeo Sharma v. State of Bihar 1998 Crl. L.J. 4596; State of U.P. v. Shambhu Nath Singh and Ors. (2001) 4 SCC 667; Kunju Muhammed alias Khumani and Anr. v. State of Kerala (2004) 9 SCC 193; Nisar Khan alias Guddu and Ors. v. State of Uttaranchal (2006) 9 SCC 386
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed as the conviction was justified based on the evidence, including the identification of the accused, recovery of stolen items, and the sequence of events as described by the prosecution.
other_sentence_order: Direction to forward a copy of the decision to all High Courts to follow the instructions issued in Rajdeo Sharma and Shambhu Nath cases by issuing appropriate circulars. Trial courts are directed to strictly adhere to the procedure prescribed under Sections 231 and 309 Cr.P.C. to ensure speedy trial.
